newsitem.title: UK: Britain says jailed nurses have appointed lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Britain says jailed nurses have appointed lawyer.

text.p: Two British nurses facing murder charges in Saudi Arabia received a visit in jail on Monday by the British consul and have chosen a lawyer to defend them, the Foreign Office said.

Deborah Kim Parry, 41, and Lucille McLauchlan, 31, have been charged with murdering Australian nurse Yvonne Gilford, 55. They were arrested on December 20, nine days after Gilford was found stabbed and beaten to death.
A Foreign Office spokesman in London said the two nurses had been visited in Damman central prison by British consul Tim Lamb, who saw them separately for 15 minutes each.
"Both women seemed in good health but were obviously concerned about the charges levelled against them," the spokesman said.

"They confirmed they were still being well treated and they have chosen a legal adviser with whom the embassy in Riyadh are already in touch. The embassy are now seeking access for their legal adviser."
It was not clear how long it would take for the lawyer to be allowed to visit the two women in jail, the spokesman said.
British consular officials intended to visit the two nurses in jail again, he said, and would assist their families if they went to Saudi Arabia.
The spokesman declined to comment on claims by Saudi newspapers on Sunday that the two women had confessed to the crime and re-enacted it to Saudi police at the scene.
The London-based al-Hayat daily quoted police as saying one of the two had confessed immediately after being arrested, while the other had done so two days later.

Western diplomats in the Gulf said the nurses had been taken to the scene of the crime at the King Fahd Military Medical Complex in the eastern Saudi city of Dhahran on December 23 where they re-enacted the crime to Saudi investigators.
The arrest of the two is diplomatically sensitive as they could, under Saudi Arabia's strict Islamic sharia laws, be executed by the sword in public, the diplomats said.
Saudi newspapers said the two women had been arrested while using the victim's cash card at a shopping mall near Dhahran.
Al-Hayat said the police found only one finger print of one of the British nurses at Gilford's flat. All other finger prints were the victim's.
On Saturday the Saudi ambassador to Britain, Dr Ghazi Algosaibi, attacked press speculation about the case and said the nurses would be given ample opportunity to defend themselves.
"These nurses were charged but must be considered innocent until the court finds them guilty...Even if found guilty, the death sentence is not automatic," he said.
